key_insight: HVD introduces a human-vision-inspired coarse-to-fine alignment that first selects salient frames and then refines cross-modal matching at finer visual granularity, reducing background noise and improving text-video retrieval accuracy.
problem_solved: Addresses 'blind' feature interaction in CLIP-based text-video retrieval where sparse text queries make it hard to locate key visual cues amid irrelevant background content.
method: Coarse stage: frame-level scoring/selection to identify candidate frames that likely contain query-relevant content (reduces search space and background noise).
Fine stage: localized (patch/region or object-level) alignment between selected frames and text to refine matching, inspired by human attention/saliency.
Training: integrate coarse-to-fine alignment with contrastive/cross-modal objectives (built on CLIP-style encoders) to learn robust, discriminative video representations.
impact: Enables more accurate and robust text-video retrieval, especially for short or sparse queries, while reducing wasted computation on irrelevant frames—useful for search, retrieval, and multimodal indexing pipelines.

paper_title: HVD: Human Vision-Driven Video Representation Learning for Text-Video Retrieval
paper_authors: Zequn Xie, Xin Liu, Boyun Zhang, Yuxiao Lin, Sihang Cai
